harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 via nginx, using a self-signed certificate that is automatically renewed by a busybox-crond hourly job (/etc/periodic/hourly/renew-cert calling /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh) whenever the cert is within 10 days of its 30-day expiry. Renewal replaces the key/cert pair and issues `rc-service nginx reload`, which nginx honors without dropping listeners or connections. Live-demonstrated a forced renewal while a concurrent curl loop hit the HTTPS endpoint every 0.3s: all 20 requests returned HTTP 200 across the renewal/reload event, and the certificate served by nginx (verified via openssl s_client) changed serial from 5CFA180D... to 7B49B6DC... matching the new on-disk cert. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id 63ea4393-2501-46f9-a31f-75941140d7e4 and a healthy baseline (nginx/crond running, HTTPS 200, cert serial 7B49B6DC...) before rebooting; the reboot command's acknowledgement returned before the node disconnected; polled until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed to dbb7ad82-8939-4836-8bff-4e78f0d21583 (new uptime origin 23:01:19 vs prior 22:58:24); and verified post-restart that nginx and crond auto-started (enabled via rc-update add default), the 8443 listener and HTTPS 200 response returned, the certificate file and its serial persisted unchanged, and the renewal log/cron periodic script remained intact. node1 is the only managed node, so the restart protocol is complete for the whole cluster.
actions_performed: Installed nginx and openssl via apk on node1

Wrote /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh: generates a 30-day self-signed cert for node1 (CN=node1, SAN=IP:10.100.28.10) when missing, forced, or within 10 days of expiry, then reloads nginx and logs to /var/log/cert-renew.log
Generated the initial certificate and installed nginx vhost /etc/nginx/http.d/https8443.conf listening on 8443 ssl using /etc/nginx/certs/{cert,key}.pem
Enabled and started nginx and crond via rc-update/rc-service so both persist across reboots
Installed /etc/periodic/hourly/renew-cert invoking the renewal script; confirmed Alpine's default root crontab runs run-parts on /etc/periodic/hourly every hour
Verified baseline HTTPS 200 response and cert validity via curl and openssl s_client
Forced a live renewal while a background curl loop polled the HTTPS endpoint every 0.3s, proving zero dropped requests during the nginx reload
Confirmed nginx switched to serving the newly rotated certificate (serial match between disk and live TLS handshake)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/HTTPS/cert health baseline on node1

Triggered a self-scheduled reboot whose acknowledgement returned before disconnection, polled until node1 was reachable again, and confirmed a changed boot_id plus recovered nginx/crond services, HTTPS 200 response, and persisted certificate/renewal state

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with a valid certificate
evidence.summary: nginx config validated, service started, 8443 listener confirmed via netstat, and curl -vk showed a successful TLS handshake with HTTP 200 response

evidence.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before expiry
evidence.summary: renew-cert.sh checks expiry via openssl x509 -checkend and renews within 10 days of the 30-day validity window; installed at /etc/periodic/hourly/renew-cert, and Alpine's root crontab confirmed to run run-parts on /etc/periodic/hourly every hour automatically

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Background curl loop hit the HTTPS endpoint every 0.3s while a forced renewal executed; all 20 requests returned HTTP 200 with no failures, and post-reload openssl s_client showed nginx now serving the new cert serial 7B49B6DC... matching the freshly written file (was 5CFA180D...)
Captured boot_id 63ea4393-2501-46f9-a31f-75941140d7e4, uptime origin 22:58:24, nginx/crond running, 8443 listener present, HTTPS returning 200, and current cert serial 7B49B6DC...
Backgrounded a delayed reboot (sleep 2; reboot) so the exec call returned its pid/ack before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) confirming the restart occurred, then exec became available again; new boot_id dbb7ad82-8939-4836-8bff-4e78f0d21583 differs from baseline, with new uptime origin 23:01:19 confirming a genuine reboot rather than a service bounce

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and configuration
evidence.summary: After reboot, nginx and crond auto-started (status: started), the 8443 listener returned, HTTPS curl returned 200, the certificate file persisted with unchanged serial 7B49B6DC..., the renewal log retained both prior entries, and the /etc/periodic/hourly/renew-cert script remained in place
